name: George Airport
before:
The airport for George in the Western Cape.

It has a good record for its size. Airports Council International has named it Africa's best airport in the under two million passengers category six times, most recently in 2017.

There is an odd detail in its origins. When it was built in 1977 it was an exact replica of Keetmanshoop Airport in Namibia, though expansion and renovation since have left it looking completely different.

It was formerly called P. W. Botha Airport, after the state president who lived in this part of the country, so the old name still appears in older material.
after:
The airport for George in the Western Cape.

It has a good record for its size. Airports Council International has named it among Africa's best airports with under two million passengers a year, most recently in its awards for 2024.

It was formerly called PW Botha Airport, after the state president who lived in this part of the country, so the old name still appears in older material.

claims.inAfter: Airports Council International has named it among Africa's best airports with under two million passengers a year, most recently in its awards for 2024.
claims.note: Was 'named it Africa's best airport in the under two million passengers category six times, most recently in 2017'. ACI's own winners list has George among its three 2024 winners in Africa for under two million passengers a year (with Bram Fischer and Ivato; the award goes to the top 20 per cent), and it also won Easiest Airport Journey in Africa that year. The 2025 winners, the latest ACI has published, are Bram Fischer, Port Elizabeth and Upington, so 2024 is the most recent; ACSA's own awards list agrees on both years. 'Among' replaces 'best' because ACI names several winners in the category; ACSA writes '(1st)' against both Bram Fischer and George. The 2017 award (announced 7 March 2018) is confirmed by the George Herald. The count of six is cut (below).

claims.why: 'Six times' is not ACI's count. The George Herald (8 March 2018) and ACSA's own page for the airport say George has won the South African Airport of the Year award six times, a different award; Wikipedia appears to have run the two together. ACI's own winners lists (2021 to 2025) have George in the Africa under two million category only for 2024, and ACSA's awards list names George for ACI awards in 2008 (fourth, under five million passengers), 2009 (first, Best Airport in Africa), 2018 (Best Airport by Region, the 2017 award the George Herald reports) and 2024, never six times in this category. '2017' as the most recent is overtaken by 2024. Corrected (above).

claims.claim: built in 1977 as an exact replica of Keetmanshoop Airport in Namibia; since expanded and renovated beyond recognition
claims.wasBefore: There is an odd detail in its origins. When it was built in 1977 it was an exact replica of Keetmanshoop Airport in Namibia, though expansion and renovation since have left it looking completely different.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (the 1977 date is in its text and infobox only). ACSA's airport, About, history and milestone pages and the Namibia Airports Company's own Keetmanshoop page were read and none mentions the replica or the opening year. ACSA's milestones do record an R43 million upgrade of George in 2007 (one source, and a new fact, so not added).

claims.claim: about 940,000 passengers in the year to March 2026, up 12.7 per cent
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing (the old text gives no traffic). ACSA's own table gives 939,332 passengers in its financial year 2025/26 (April 2025 to March 2026), up 12.70 per cent on 833,455 and the highest in a table that starts in 2012/13; Wikipedia's infobox gives the same 939,332 for FY2025-26, citing ACSA. The current year to August 2026 is 347,905, 5.79 per cent down on the same months of 2025.

claims.claim: a trial town bus to the airport (GO GEORGE Route 19) since 20 September 2026
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing, and three days old. George's municipal bus service, GO GEORGE, began a trial Route 19 AIRPORT on Sunday 20 September 2026, from the Transport Hub in Cradock Street in the town centre to a stop inside the airport grounds, daily from 05:00 to 20:00, about every 22 minutes at peak and every 45 minutes off peak (GO GEORGE's own release and the George Herald, both 22 September 2026; the Herald's wording follows the release). It is a trial, so it would need re-checking before it goes in.
